expectation: I expect the sieve to separate the regolith by particle size, though I don't know what material the game will produce.

effect: Sieving produced a consistent fine feedstock, so the furnace can test material with fewer large stones.
reaction: The explanation makes the purpose of grading clear; I’m curious what the furnace trial will produce.
reason: The furnace trial is the only available combination and seems like the next step toward making paving.

effect: The furnace produced usable porous bricks after a slower firing cycle, and the new goal is to lay a workshop floor.
reaction: The failed first trial makes the firing process more interesting and shows why the cycle matters.
reason: Placing the fired bricks on the workshop ground seems like the direct way to make the solid floor.
expectation: I expect to lay the bricks as a workshop floor and complete the new goal, though other construction may still be needed.

effect: The bricks made a level workshop floor, completing the chapter and giving the workbench a stable base.
reaction: The detail about the bench staying put makes the floor’s practical value satisfying.

mostWorthwhile.text: The furnace trial was most worthwhile: the failed edge and slower successful cycle made the material’s behavior feel consequential.

leastWorthwhile.text: Making the sieve and using it were straightforward, predictable steps, though the later explanation gave them a purpose.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the first firing trial flaked and that a slower cycle produced sound, porous bricks.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary; the sequence from excavation and screening to firing and paving had a clear purpose.

continue.text: Yes. I’d be curious to see how the remaining bricks and local ceramic feedstock support the food-growing work mentioned in the chapter introduction.
